problems.source_says: The paper separately rates the quality of the submitted text, assessing readability, categorization and logical coherence. Section 6 of the supplied codebook explicitly includes quality of a single output under usefulness, so this output-quality rating should be coded usefulness rather than the residual other category. Being supplementary and excluded from the creativity composite does not change that construct mapping.
problems.quote:
Text Quality (Supplementary Indicator, 1–7): Evaluate whether the text is clearly categorized,
readable, and logically coherent.
problems.locator: PDF p. 24 (SI p. 6), S1.6, Text Quality rubric; PDF p. 8, Human-rated creativity, lines 275-277; creativity-codebook.md, section 6, Construct table, usefulness and other rows (lines 79 and 85).

confirmed.statement: Criterion 3 holds: four experts independently rated every individual proposal in submitted team documents, blind to condition. These are output ratings, not participant self-reports.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 21 (SI p. 3), S1.1, product-design experts; PDF pp. 23-24 (SI pp. 5-6), S1.6.

confirmed.statement: S1-O1 combines originality, appropriateness and elaboration with weights 0.70, 0.15 and 0.15; originality combines quality, quantity and naming. Scores are averaged within teams and across four raters, with rater-severity calibration.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 8, lines 269-284; PDF p. 24, S1.6; PDF p. 64 (SI p. 46), Supplementary Figure 4 caption.

confirmed.statement: S1-O2 assesses novelty and non-obviousness; S1-O3 is the originality composite; S1-O4 assesses usefulness and feasibility; S1-O5 assesses detail and development. Their novelty, novelty, usefulness and elaboration codes and expert-rater measurement are supported.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 24 (SI p. 6), S1.6 rubric; PDF p. 8, lines 269-282.

confirmed.statement: S1-O6 is a separate 1-7 expert rating of the final text and is excluded from the creativity composite; its output status and measurement description are supported despite its construct error.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 8, lines 275-277; PDF p. 24 (SI p. 6), S1.6, Text Quality rubric.

confirmed.statement: S1-O7 uses mean pairwise TF-IDF distances among paragraph-level idea units within each team document. Its lexical measure and flexibility coding describe within-output variety; it does not measure similarity across different people or teams.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 9, Process and mechanism measures, lines 298-299; PDF p. 17, Figure 3a caption; codebook section 6, Construct.

confirmed.statement: S1-O8 counts separate final proposal units in each team submission, supporting fluency and category_count. It differs from the deduplicated valid-feature count used inside originality.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 9, lines 300-301; PDF p. 8, lines 278-280; PDF p. 24, Originality-Quantity rubric.

confirmed.statement: S1-O9 is automated creativity scoring of the same proposals by ten named LLM raters, aggregated for the team-level ai_pool_z_all10 outcome; its secondary diagnostic status is explicit.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 8, Data sources, lines 259-267; PDF p. 26 (SI p. 8), S1.9; PDF p. 48, Supplementary Table 22.

confirmed.statement: S1-O10 is final-document character length, supporting elaboration under the codebook. The paper reports team-level means; leaving measure null avoids inventing a measurement category absent from the codebook.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 41 (SI p. 23), Supplementary Table 15, Final proposal characters column and caption; codebook section 6, elaboration and Measure definitions.

confirmed.statement: The ten recorded outcome analyses use teams, with 148 teams overall. Analysis counts are 30 teams each in C1-C3 and 29 each in C4-C5; proposal-level reliability observations are not the treatment-analysis unit.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 21, S1.1; PDF p. 27, Supplementary Table 1; PDF pp. 31-36, 41-42 and 48, Supplementary Tables 5-10, 15-16 and 22.

confirmed.statement: AI access was Stage 1 only in C1/C5, Stage 2 only in C2, all stages in C3 and never in C4. Disabled-stage access was blocked, and the logs show no off-window AI use; mixed availability records this phase-restricted design.
confirmed.locator: PDF pp. 22-23, S1.2 and S1.4; PDF p. 63 (SI p. 45), Supplementary Figure 3 caption.

confirmed.statement: The scored proposals were developed in one continuing 40-minute task, with personal drafting before final consolidation and submission. With_ai/immediate is supported for these jointly developed outputs; no separately scored output produced wholly after AI removal is reported.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 8, lines 251-257; PDF pp. 21-22, S1.1-S1.2; PDF p. 23, S1.4. Full markdown, including the complete supplement, reviewed.

confirmed.statement: All 49 reported entries match their cited PDF tables, including arm means, reported SDs and team counts, mean differences, Hedges g, confidence limits, and all 36 timing-model rows with coefficients, HC3 SEs, p values and N.
confirmed.locator: PDF pp. 27, 31-36, 41-42 and 48: Supplementary Tables 1, 5-10, 15-16 and 22. Checked by direct PDF text extraction and field comparisons.

confirmed.statement: The form correctly leaves Table 15 parenthetical dispersion unidentified. The caption does not specify SD versus SE; it also correctly identifies the printed Stage-1 elaboration p=0 as rounded.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 41, Supplementary Table 15 caption; PDF p. 35, Supplementary Table 9, Elaboration/Stage-1 row.

confirmed.statement: The six human-rating ICCs, expert-only and mixed-model sensitivity numbers, AI-pool ICC=0.853, and AI-human correlation range 0.202-0.389 over 394 proposals agree with the cited tables.
Originality-quantity and naming novelty are separately scored rubric components documented within S1-O1/S1-O3; no standalone condition estimates for either are reported in the dimension tables.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 24, S1.6 rubric and composite formula; PDF pp. 32-36, Supplementary Tables 6-10; forms/c370.json, S1-O1 and S1-O3 measure_detail.

confirmed.statement: Additional document idea-unit count appears only as a boundary-check predictor of already-recorded human creativity. AI provenance compares proposals with AI content, and AI-human divergence compares evaluations of the same outputs; neither supplies an omitted across_people diversity outcome.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 68, Supplementary Figure 8d caption; PDF p. 9, Semantic provenance; PDF p. 52, Supplementary Table 26 caption; PDF p. 70, Supplementary Figure 10d caption.

summary: S1-O6 codes text quality as other, although the codebook places quality of a single output under usefulness. Criterion 3 holds because experts rated submitted proposals, and all 49 recorded statistical entries match their cited PDF tables.
